text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.

The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of God; Nebuchadnezzar carried them off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his own god, and put the vessels in his god's treasury.
Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some of the people of Israel, both of the royal family and of the nobility,

young men without blemish, handsome, skilled in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge, understanding learning, and competent to stand in the king's palace — to be taught the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
The king assigned them a daily portion of the food and wine that came from his own table, to be trained for three years, after which they were to stand before the king.
Among these young men, from the tribe of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The chief of the eunuchs renamed them: Daniel he called Belteshazzar, Hananiah he called Shadrach, Mishael he called Meshach, and Azariah he called Abednego.
But Daniel resolved in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's food or wine, and he asked the chief of the eunuchs to let him avoid it.
God had already given Daniel favor and compassion in the eyes of the chief of the eunuchs,

who nonetheless said to Daniel, "I fear my lord the king, who set your food and drink; why should he see your faces look worse than the other young men your age? You would put my head at risk with the king."
So Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had placed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
"Please test your servants for ten days; give us only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare our appearance with that of the young men who eat the king's food, and deal with your servants according to what you see."
The steward agreed to this request and tested them for ten days.
At the end of the ten days they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who had eaten the king's food.
So the steward continued to take away their rich food and wine and gave them vegetables instead.
To these four young men God gave learning and skill in all literature and wisdom, and Daniel besides had understanding of every kind of vision and dream.
At the end of the time the king had set for their training, the chief of the eunuchs brought all the young men before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke with them, and none among them all was found equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, so they entered the king's service.
In every matter calling for wisdom and understanding, the king found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
